h1: TDEE - Total Daily Energy Expenditure Calculator
summary: Supply the body fat, the age, the height and the lean Body Mass and the TDEE - Total Daily Energy Expenditure calculator solves for basal metabolic rate (BMR) (Results). It is built for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the TDEE - Total Daily Energy Expenditure calculator work?
sections.html:
The TDEE - Total Daily Energy Expenditure calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports basal metabolic rate (BMR) (Results) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the BMR formula, the sex and the physical activity level (PAL)); then you type in the body fat, the age (18-120), the height and the lean Body Mass (About you).

Press Calculate once and the page holds the relationship, tracking which boxes you filled and working out everything else; from that point on it follows every edit you make.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the TDEE - Total Daily Energy Expenditure calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Basal metabolic rate (BMR)=rounded, (-5 × age (18-120) + 625 × height + 10 × weight + 5)
Basal metabolic rate (BMR)=rounded, ((108 ÷ 5) × lean body mass + 370)
Basal metabolic rate (BMR)=rounded, (-5677 ÷ 1000 × age (18-120) + (4799 ÷ 10) × height + (13397 ÷ 1000) × weight + 44181 ÷ 500)
Basal metabolic rate (BMR)=rounded, (-433 ÷ 100 × age (18-120) + (1549 ÷ 5) × height + (9247 ÷ 1000) × weight + 447593 ÷ 1000)
Basal metabolic rate (BMR)=rounded, (-1351 ÷ 200 × age (18-120) + (50033 ÷ 100) × height + (34379 ÷ 2500) × weight + 66473 ÷ 1000)
Basal metabolic rate (BMR)=rounded, (-11689 ÷ 2500 × age (18-120) + (4624 ÷ 25) × height + (47817 ÷ 5000) × weight + 1310191 ÷ 2000)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories
  • Energy, opening in kilocalories

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The TDEE - Total Daily Energy Expenditure calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the body fat, the age and the height — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the TDEE - Total Daily Energy Expenditure calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns basal metabolic rate (BMR) (Results), derived from the body fat, the age and the height. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the TDEE - Total Daily Energy Expenditure calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the body fat, the age, the height and the lean Body Mass, which is 9 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter height in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Height opens in centimeters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (4 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the TDEE - Total Daily Energy Expenditure calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
